_README: TEMPLATE — copy this file, delete what you don't need, and edit the rest.
Keys starting with _ are ignored by the runner; they exist because JSON has no comments.
Three sections, and the difference is load-bearing:
setup    — preconditions. A failure here ABORTS the flow before steps run,
because a test whose preconditions did not hold cannot produce
teardown — cleanup. ALWAYS runs, including after a failure, and never
'name' is used for report filenames, visual baseline keys, and run-history
grouping. Keep it stable across runs or you lose your trend data.
'intent' is optional but write it on anything that might drift: when the
selector breaks, it is what the healer uses to find the element you meant.
EVERY FLOW NEEDS AN ASSERTION. A flow that only clicks and navigates passes
whether or not the feature works — worse than no test, because it displaces
the manual check that would have caught the bug.
name: template — rename me
_setup: Preconditions. Storage is origin-scoped, so goto MUST come first.

steps._: --- navigation and interaction ---

steps.intent: the eligibility rules table
the More filters button above the table
the search box in the filter panel

steps._: One step for any dropdown — a native <select> OR a custom combobox. 'value' is the option's VISIBLE LABEL. Never fill a dropdown, and never click it open to guess: this opens it and picks.
steps.intent: the status filter dropdown

steps._: check/uncheck verify the state actually CHANGED — prefer them over click when the point is the resulting state. Works on native checkboxes/radios and on aria-checked/aria-pressed toggles.
steps.intent: the include-archived filter

steps._: Types key by key, firing real keyboard events — for autocomplete/typeahead/masked fields that fill() cannot wake. Use fill everywhere else; it is faster.
steps.intent: the assignee typeahead

steps._: Hands the browser to the LLM agent until the goal is met. Use it to REACH a page, never to assert. Costs tokens; needs the agent role configured.
steps.goal: Navigate to the benefits eligibility rules admin page. Only click navigation links; do not submit or delete anything.

steps._: --- keyboard and focus ---
selector is optional — omit it to press on the page rather than an element.
steps.intent: submit the search with the keyboard
focus stays in the search box after submitting

steps._: Tabs from the top of the document and asserts focus lands in this order. Cannot be produced by `wowlidator author` — hand-write it.
--- assertions: the point of the test ---
CONTAINS, not equals.
steps.intent: the record count line under the table
the results table

steps._: expectHidden and expectCount:0 deliberately SKIP healing — repairing a selector whose whole purpose is to not resolve would turn a correct pass into a meaningless one.
steps.intent: no error banner is shown
the search button
pagination on the first page
8 data rows plus the header row

steps._: CONTAINS, not equals.
EQUALS, exactly.
steps.intent: the search box keeps what was typed

steps._: EQUALS, exactly.
steps.name: aria-invalid
steps.intent: the search box is not flagged invalid

steps._: --- backend: HTTP the test makes itself ---

Sent through the BROWSER, so it carries whatever session the UI steps above established — log in through the real login form once and these calls are that user. A non-2xx does NOT fail this step; expectStatus is where a status becomes pass/fail, which is what lets you test error paths. 'save' keeps a value for later steps to use as {{name}}.
steps.intent: Create an order for this test to work with

steps._: A request nobody asserts on proves nothing — it passes whether the endpoint returns the right data or a 500.
steps.intent: The order was created

steps._: {{orderId}} came from the 'save' above. An unknown variable fails the step rather than silently becoming an empty string.
Omit 'value' to assert only that the path EXISTS — right for a server-assigned id whose exact value you cannot know.
steps.intent: The API stored what the UI said it did

steps._: --- boundary-value analysis ---

One field, many values, an assertion after each. EVERY case runs even after one fails — a partial boundary table is far less useful than the whole one. 'submit' is load-bearing: validation usually fires on submit, not on input, so without it every case asserts against a form that never ran. Cannot be produced by `wowlidator author` — hand-write it.
steps.intent: the quantity field

steps._: --- visual regression ---

First run CREATES the baseline and passes, saying nothing was verified. Keyed by flow name + snapshot name, so inserting a step earlier does not invalidate it. Re-baseline with: wowlidator run my.flow.json --update-baselines
steps.name: rules-table

_teardown: Always runs, even after a failure. Never masks the real error.
